A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PTQ1.61 and contain the complete 20-page paper, including Appendices A-F. Text, equations, figures, and tables support reliable comparison after matching renumbered and relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantization experiments on LLaMA and OPT, including perplexity, reasoning accuracy, component ablations, and additional appendix evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds full-precision reasoning references and a comparison of pretrained and preprocessed full-precision models.

M1.justification: The structured mask, block-wise scaling optimization, losses, and restorative LoRA procedure remain unchanged. Describing preprocessing as optional clarifies an existing variant: v1 already evaluates PTQ1.61 without preprocessing in Table 6.

E1.justification: Training corpora, evaluation datasets, and task types are retained, including WikiText2, C4, reasoning benchmarks, MMLU, GSM8K, and LongBench. The removed LLaMA-3-70B configuration changes model-size coverage rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds FP16 reference comparators to its reasoning comparisons. Full-precision comparisons existed elsewhere in v1, but were absent from this table. The existing quantized comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the stated LoRA preprocessing budget from 10K steps and rank 32 to 20K steps and rank 64. Table 1 removes LLaMA-3-70B, and new Table 9 adds full-precision preprocessing controls. Calibration and metrics remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix D.2 and Table 9 examine whether preprocessing improves quantizability despite worsening full-precision performance. This adds a targeted control alongside previously reported quantized outcomes. Existing component, mask, angular-bias, and sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No seed-count, repeated-run, or uncertainty-reporting information is added.

E6.justification: v2 adds FP16 reasoning entries and preprocessed FP16 LLaMA-13B perplexities of 9.32 on WikiText2 and 12.33 on C4. It removes the LLaMA-3-70B results, including PTQ1.61 perplexities of 28.26 and 37.34. Retained quantized scores match; Table 9's quantized outcomes already appeared in v1 Table 6.

T1.justification: The quantization definitions, error-bound reasoning, and bit-width derivation are retained. Equation 9 receives prime and multiplication-notation corrections without changing the mathematical operation or introducing new reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about effective 1.61-bit quantization, structured masks, learned scaling factors, preprocessing, and state-of-the-art performance.

C2.justification: Section 3.4 and new Appendix D.2 explicitly distinguish improving quantizability from improving full-precision inference performance. Section 4.5 clarifies that preprocessing is optional because of its runtime cost. Existing runtime and hardware limitations remain.

D1.justification: The documented LoRA step count and rank are revised from 10K/32 to 20K/64. Other calibration, optimizer, hardware, runtime, and code-access information is retained. The revision is not identified as either a correction or a newly executed training configuration.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to prior PTQ, PEFT, and QAT methods are retained. Reference pagination changes do not add or remove related research.

P1.justification: v2 adds localized clarification paragraphs, Appendix D.2, and a funding acknowledgment, and moves the mention of additional benchmarks into the experimental setup. Most prose and the overall section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 loses a column, Table 2 gains FP16 rows, and new Table 9 causes subsequent tables to be renumbered and content to reflow. Figures are unchanged. v2 also introduces an unexplained 1-7 to 1-8 label change in Table 2 and a stray 4 beside an OmniQuant entry in Table 1.

improvement.justification: The added FP16 reasoning references and Table 9 modestly improve evaluation transparency and support the preprocessing rationale: full-precision performance worsens while quantized performance improves. These useful controls provide a limited overall gain, tempered by removed LLaMA-3-70B evidence, unexplained training-setting revisions with unchanged retained scores, and new table ambiguities.
